questions.q: A key is stored on N = 3 replicas. Which read/write quorum makes a read overlap the latest acknowledged write (in the normal case)?
questions.why: R + W > N: 2 + 2 > 3, so the replicas you read and the ones that acked the write share at least one. It isn't full linearizability: sloppy quorums and concurrent writes can still surprise you.

questions.q: With consistent hashing, you add a 5th node to a 4-node ring. About how many keys move?
questions.why: Only the keys the new node takes over move: about 1/(n+1). With hash(key) mod n, changing n moves most keys.

questions.q: A crawler's Bloom filter says a URL was already seen. What can be true?
choices: It may never have been seen (a false positive), so the crawler might skip a new page
questions.why: Bloom filters can give false positives, never false negatives. About 10 bits per URL gives ~1% false positives.

questions.q: A Count-Min Sketch estimates how often each ad was clicked. Its error is…
questions.why: Hash collisions only add counts. Fine for a top-K dashboard; billing needs exact counts.

questions.q: A Kafka topic has 6 partitions and a consumer group has 10 consumers. What happens?
questions.why: In a classic consumer group each partition goes to at most one consumer. To scale consumers, add partitions.

questions.q: Billing must count each ad click exactly once, but the log delivers at least once. What gives exact results?
choices: Dedup by click id and make the writes idempotent
questions.why: At-least-once delivery + idempotent processing gives effectively-once results. Late events also need a watermark or allowed lateness.

questions.q: 360k online drivers send a GPS position every 4 s, and only the latest matters. Where does it go?
choices: A new SQL row per update
In memory, overwriting each driver's latest position
questions.why: 90k writes/s of values that are stale in seconds: an in-memory store keyed by driver, partitioned by region, not a durable row each time.

questions.q: A crawler fetches 770 pages/s and each fetch takes about 1 s. How many fetches must be in flight?
questions.why: Little's law: in flight = rate × time = 770 × 1 s. Throughput comes from many concurrent connections, not faster servers.
